topics.citation: USDA SNAP FY 2026 COLA Memo — Income Eligibility Standards (Oct. 1, 2025 – Sept. 30, 2026)
topics.heading: SNAP income eligibility standards, FY 2026 — gross (130% FPL), net (100% FPL), and separate-elderly-disabled (165% FPL) monthly limits by household size
topics.text: SNAP income eligibility standards effective October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2026, from USDA's FY 2026 Cost-of-Living Adjustments memorandum. GROSS monthly income limits (130 percent of poverty), 48 states, D.C., Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands: household of 1 $1,696; 2 $2,292; 3 $2,888; 4 $3,483; 5 $4,079; 6 $4,675; 7 $5,271; 8 $5,867; each additional member +$596. Alaska gross (130%): 1 $2,118; 2 $2,864; 3 $3,609; 4 $4,354; 5 $5,100; 6 $5,845; 7 $6,590; 8 $7,336; each additional +$746. Hawaii gross (130%): 1 $1,949; 2 $2,635; 3 $3,321; 4 $4,007; 5 $4,692; 6 $5,378; 7 $6,064; 8 $6,750; each additional +$686. NET monthly income limits (100 percent of poverty), 48 states, D.C., Guam, Virgin Islands: 1 $1,305; 2 $1,763; 3 $2,221; 4 $2,680; 5 $3,138; 6 $3,596; 7 $4,055; 8 $4,513; each additional +$459. Alaska net: 1 $1,630; 2 $2,203; 3 $2,776; 4 $3,350; 5 $3,923; 6 $4,496; 7 $5,070; 8 $5,643; each additional +$574. Hawaii net: 1 $1,500; 2 $2,027; 3 $2,555; 4 $3,082; 5 $3,610; 6 $4,137; 7 $4,665; 8 $5,192; each additional +$528. Gross limits for households where elderly/disabled members are a separate household (165 percent of poverty), 48 states, D.C., Guam, Virgin Islands: 1 $2,152; 2 $2,909; 3 $3,665; 4 $4,421; 5 $5,177; 6 $5,934; 7 $6,690; 8 $7,446; each additional +$757; Alaska: 1 $2,689; 2 $3,635; 3 $4,581; 4 $5,527; 5 $6,473; 6 $7,419; 7 $8,365; 8 $9,311; +$946; Hawaii: 1 $2,474; 2 $3,344; 3 $4,215; 4 $5,085; 5 $5,956; 6 $6,826; 7 $7,696; 8 $8,567; +$871. These are the dollar tables that 7 CFR 273.9(a)'s percentages point at. States using broad-based categorical eligibility (BBCE) may apply a higher gross limit (up to 200 percent of poverty) and their own asset rules; the state's own published figures govern there.

topics.heading: SNAP maximum and minimum monthly allotments, FY 2026, by household size and area
topics.text: SNAP maximum monthly allotments effective October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2026, from USDA's FY 2026 Cost-of-Living Adjustments memorandum. 48 states and D.C.: household of 1 $298; 2 $546; 3 $785; 4 $994; 5 $1,183; 6 $1,421; 7 $1,571; 8 $1,789; each additional person +$218. Guam: 1 $439; 2 $806; 3 $1,157; 4 $1,465; 5 $1,743; 6 $2,095; 7 $2,315; 8 $2,637; +$322. U.S. Virgin Islands: 1 $383; 2 $703; 3 $1,009; 4 $1,278; 5 $1,521; 6 $1,827; 7 $2,019; 8 $2,300; +$281. Alaska (Urban): 1 $385; 2 $707; 3 $1,015; 4 $1,285; 5 $1,529; 6 $1,838; 7 $2,031; 8 $2,314; +$282. Alaska (Rural 1): 1 $491; 2 $901; 3 $1,295; 4 $1,639; 5 $1,950; 6 $2,344; 7 $2,590; 8 $2,950; +$360. Alaska (Rural 2): 1 $598; 2 $1,097; 3 $1,576; 4 $1,995; 5 $2,374; 6 $2,853; 7 $3,152; 8 $3,591; +$438. Hawaii: 1 $506; 2 $929; 3 $1,334; 4 $1,689; 5 $2,010; 6 $2,415; 7 $2,668; 8 $3,040; +$371. MINIMUM monthly allotment for eligible households of 1–2 people: $24 in the 48 states and D.C.; $35 Guam; $31 U.S. Virgin Islands; $31 Alaska Urban; $39 Alaska Rural 1; $48 Alaska Rural 2; $41 Hawaii. The actual benefit is the maximum allotment for the household size minus 30 percent of the household's net income (7 CFR 273.10(e)); the maximum is what a household with no net income receives.

topics.citation: USDA SNAP FY 2026 COLA Memo — Deductions (Oct. 1, 2025 – Sept. 30, 2026)
topics.heading: SNAP standard deductions, excess-shelter caps, and homeless shelter deduction, FY 2026, by area
topics.text: SNAP deduction amounts effective October 1, 2025 through September 30, 2026, from USDA's FY 2026 Cost-of-Living Adjustments memorandum. STANDARD DEDUCTION by household size — 48 states and D.C.: sizes 1–2 $209; 3 $209; 4 $223; 5 $261; 6+ $299. Alaska: sizes 1–4 $358; 5 $358; 6+ $374. Hawaii: sizes 1–4 $295; 5 $300; 6+ $344. Guam: sizes 1–3 $420; 4 $445; 5 $522; 6+ $598. U.S. Virgin Islands: sizes 1–2 $184; 3 $185; 4 $223; 5 $261; 6+ $299. MAXIMUM EXCESS SHELTER DEDUCTION (the shelter cap, which does not apply to households with an elderly or disabled member): $744 in the 48 states and D.C.; $1,189 Alaska; $1,003 Hawaii; $873 Guam; $586 U.S. Virgin Islands. MAXIMUM HOMELESS SHELTER DEDUCTION: $198.99 in every area. The earned income deduction remains 20 percent of earned income, and the excess shelter deduction covers shelter costs above half of income after other deductions (7 CFR 273.9(d)).
